items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Charlie DuPont and myself had the business.

ctx.x: Okay, you played the record for Air Ruffin.

And, uh, he says, I know who that is. So, he told us, that's a kid from Davenport by the name of Bix. He didn't call him Bix, he called him Leon, his right name. Right. So, that's a kid from Davenport by the name of Leon Bodyback. He didn't know who the rest of the band was, because he didn't know any of them. Outside, yeah, he did know that, he knew the banjo player, who was the same banjo player who played with the Wolverines, Louis Black. And, uh, he taught, and the thing, the trumpet solo, well, in fact, the…
And all that when he was only 21, huh?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: A fella by the name of Charlie DuPont and I kind of helped them out a little bit until they could get some money from California to get back home

ctx.x: Well, some of the earlier things he did, as you heard, were very melodic, lyrical.

Later, he got more frenzied as he got into another kind of music. Well, you changed like that. I've seen bands do that. I've seen bands make a national reputation playing one style. And the minute they get in the money, they changed the band around and play all together different. And it synced. Kenton is one that did that. He got more wild and more wild as he was. There's a funny thing about Kenton. I was out in California in 1934 to 1938 with Gene Austin. And I went down to Balboa Beach. And there had a bunch…
